name: fynd-dyrka
description: Security review in seven layers: SAST, secrets, dependencies, IaC, DAST, external recon of a live service (exposed .git and other sensitive paths, secrets in production JS, security headers/CORS/HTTP methods, a bounded crawl for reflected-XSS/SQLi candidates, open ports via Shodan and an active nmap check, mail spoofability via SPF/DMARC, domain WHOIS expiry and VirusTotal reputation), an optional explicitly-scoped social-engineering layer, and platform — the real state of the production deployment (public database address, runtime variables, deploy permissions, backups, config drift from the repository). Orchestrates semgrep/gitleaks/osv-scanner/trivy/nuclei and does what scanners cannot: reading code for logic flaws (auth bypass, IDOR, SSRF, races over money) confirmed by running them, a separate pass on availability and cost (missing rate limits, unbounded queries, ReDoS, cost-DoS on paid APIs) and on observability (will an incident leave a trace), MITRE mapping and attack-chain construction. It also covers the agentic surface (LLM agents, MCP servers, RAG): excessive agency, tool poisoning, memory isolation, prompt injection. Every HIGH/CRITICAL finding is put through an attempt to refute it, not only to confirm it.
